interfaces.phase_evolution: κ-carbides precipitate in austenitic steels on the existing short-range order during aging

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Far more ductile and stretchable than conventional automotive sheet steel grades DP800 and TRIP780 (which have even slightly lower strength); austenitic low-density steels are highly ductile because of ductility-enhancing mechanisms.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Solution-treatment step of the 'Solutionized and aged' processing condition for the austenitic steel in Table I; no specific temperature is reported for this step.
Aging step of the 'Solutionized and aged' condition; aging precipitates κ-carbides on the existing short-range order in the austenite.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Literature tensile properties (Table I); TE and n marked 'b' were determined by the current authors from data in the corresponding reference.

phases_present.morphology: concentrated solid solution with short-range ordering usually present

precipitates.distribution: can precipitate both intergranularly and intragranularly in austenite; intragranular precipitates are believed to be effective in increasing the yield strength significantly

structures.overall_structure: Concentrated solid solution of austenite (austenitic low-density steel); short-range ordering usually takes place in the austenite; κ-carbides precipitate on the existing short-range order during aging

unmapped_findings: Strain hardening exponent n = 0.29 (marked 'b' in Table I, i.e., determined by the current authors from the data in the corresponding reference) is reported for the Austenitic Fe-30.5Mn-8Al-1.2C steel, solutionized and aged.
The normal anisotropy factor (r̄) is not reported (shown as '-') for this sample in Table I.
The tensile-property data row for this sample in Table I is attributed to reference 58.
Austenitic low-density steels, to which this sample belongs, are very high (>25 wt.%) Mn-containing Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys; the present alloy Fe-30.5Mn-8Al-1.2C contains 30.5 wt.% Mn.
